findings.summary: The seed acceptance requires explicit conflict ownership, but the seed and implementation packets contain no `Conflict Domain` declaration or equivalent field. Existing issue-tracker policy explicitly treats Conflict Domain as a scheduling and overlap-control contract, so non-overlapping ownership cannot be deterministically verified from these packets.

The completion predicate conflicts with the existing operating contract: the seed says the issue-owning agent releases it as `complete` immediately before maintainer review, while the issue-tracker contract says `agent-work release` moves a green packet to `ready-for-human`, and completion is recorded after merge. The required status transition and authority boundary are therefore not deterministic.

The phrase “Exactly the role-assurance PRD, this seed packet, and issues 05–08 exist as the planning payload” is not operationally precise: the repository already contains other harness-integrity packets and multiple evidence directories. The acceptance needs a scoped definition (for example, exact changed planning paths) to make deterministic validation possible.

residualRisks: Dependency and status synchronization may pass while concurrent-work conflict ownership remains unenforced.
Different agents may legitimately choose incompatible complete versus ready-for-human transitions.
A validator cannot distinguish intended planning-payload scope from an exact repository-file count.
